title: Writing Interfaces
concept: Define interfaces with method signatures describing what implementors must provide — the blueprint for type capabilities.
why: Well-designed interfaces are the foundation of reusable code. They define clear contracts that types must fulfill.
tips: Name interfaces as adjectives or capabilities: Comparable, Display, Clone
Keep interfaces small — 1-3 methods is ideal; 5+ is a red flag
Use Self to refer to the implementing type in method signatures
Each interface method should have one clear purpose
common_mistakes: Designing interfaces too large — split into smaller, composable interfaces
Making interfaces too specific to one use case — they should be reusable
Methods with unclear semantics — 'process' could mean anything; be specific
